info.title: Terramantle API
info.summary: Private Terraform & OpenTofu registry, state backend, plan gate and provider supply chain.
info.description:
Terramantle is a private registry and governance plane for Terraform / OpenTofu. One Cloudflare
Worker serves every surface below, which is why they share one spec:

| Surface | Prefix | Spoken by |
|---|---|---|
| Service discovery | `/.well-known/` | `terraform` / `tofu`, the CLI, the portal SPA |
| Registry Protocol v1 — modules | `/v1/modules/` | `terraform` / `tofu` |
| Registry Protocol v1 — providers | `/v1/providers/` | `terraform` / `tofu` |
| State backend (HTTP) | `/state/{org}/` | the `http` state backend |
| Plan ingest | `/plans/{org}/` | CI, after `terraform show -json` |
| Management API | `/api/` | the portal SPA, the `terramantle` CLI, CI |
| Internal ingest | `/internal/`, `/api/internal/` | scanners, the Argo build fleet, OPA |

## Getting started

1. **Discover.** `GET /.well-known/terramantle-cli.json` returns the OIDC issuer, the audience
   every token must carry, and the public device-flow client id. Nothing else needs to be
   configured out of band. The portal's equivalent is
   `GET /.well-known/terramantle-portal.json`.
2. **Get a token.** Humans run authorization-code + PKCE against the portal application
   (`oidcPortal`); the CLI runs the device grant against its own application; CI either mints a
   machine `client_credentials` token or presents its native GitHub/GitLab OIDC token (see
   `vcsOidc`). Every token must carry the registry audience — request the `terramantle` scope
   or the Worker rejects the bearer on `aud`.
3. **Call the API.** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Terraform's `http` state backend cannot
   send a bearer, so the state and plan surfaces also accept HTTP Basic with the token in the
   password half (`basicAuth`).

## Conventions

- Collections are plural nouns; the HTTP method carries the verb. The few RPC-shaped
  exceptions are explicit state transitions on a resource (`.../rescan`, `.../promote`,
  `.../approve`) and are documented as such.
- Request and response bodies are `application/json` unless stated. Timestamps are
  **epoch milliseconds** (integer), matching the D1 columns behind them.
- Filtering, paging and sorting go in query parameters (`limit`, `offset`, …); identity goes
  in the path.
- Errors are a flat `{ "error": "<machine_code>", "message": "<human text>" }`
  (`#/components/schemas/Error`). The `error` code is the stable contract — match on it, not
  on `message`. Two surfaces deliberately differ: the Registry Protocol routes answer
  `{ "errors": [...] }` as HashiCorp's protocol requires
  (`#/components/schemas/RegistryErrors`), and a tier limit answers `402` with
  `#/components/schemas/QuotaExceeded`.

## Status codes used across the API

| Code | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| `200` / `201` / `204` | Success. `204` is also the Registry Protocol's module-download response, and "no state yet". |
| `202` | Accepted but not finished — a publish that was still scanning when the client's `wait` budget ran out. |
| `400` | Malformed request: bad JSON, a missing required field, an unparseable version constraint. |
| `401` | No credential, or one that failed validation. |
| `402` | A plan/tier limit was hit. Not a failure — see `QuotaExceeded`. |
| `403` | Authenticated but not allowed: wrong role, not a member, a bot on a human-only action, a blocked artefact. |
| `404` | Not found, or a feature kill-switch is off, or an artefact deliberately hidden (`serve_mode: block`). |
| `405` | Right path, wrong method on the protocol routers. |
| `409` | Conflict: a concurrent claim, or a duplicate. |
| `410` | Endpoint removed. The body names its replacement. |
| `413` | Body over the surface's cap (100 MB state/plan, 10 MB lock file). |
| `422` | Well-formed but semantically rejected (unknown tier, unsupported upstream, unresolvable source repo). |
| `423` | Locked: the policy gate blocked this workspace's next apply. |
| `429` | Rate limited (the policy-settings debounce). |
| `500` | Unhandled. |
| `502` | A dependency the Worker fronts failed (upstream registry, queue send). |
| `503` | Feature not enabled, or a required binding/credential is unconfigured. |

## Companions

- **Queue contracts.** The asynchronous half of the platform — every Cloudflare Queue message
  between the Worker, the scanners and the Argo build fleet — is specified in AsyncAPI 3.0 at
  `packages/queue-contracts/asyncapi.yaml`, served from `GET /asyncapi.json`.
- **Policy input.** The JSON Schema for the OPA policy `input` document is served live from
  `GET /api/policy-schema` — it is generated from the Worker's own types, so it is the
  authority for policy authors rather than anything restated here.

servers.description: Production. Serves every surface in this spec.

Org-scoped provider registry. `GET /.well-known/terraform.json` on this host advertises
`providers.v1: /v1/providers/{orgSlug}/`, so `tofu` appends provider sources to the
org-scoped route. The subdomain is a ROUTING hint only and never authenticates anything —
membership is still enforced per request. Only the Registry Protocol is served here; the
`/api/*` management layer stays on the bare host.

tags.name: Discovery
tags.description:
Unauthenticated bootstrap documents. Everything a client needs to find the IdP, the
audience and its own client id, so none of it is baked into a binary or a bundle.

tags.name: Registry — Modules
tags.description:
Terraform Registry Protocol v1 for modules, plus the Terramantle-specific publish,
deprecate, block and serve-override operations on the same resources.

tags.name: Registry — Providers
tags.description:
Terraform Registry Protocol v1 for providers: the version list, the per-platform download
document, and the artifact files. Two path families — org-scoped (`/{orgSlug}/…`, preferred)
and token-scoped (legacy, org resolved from the token).

tags.name: State Backend

The `http` state backend protocol: `GET`/`POST` state, `LOCK`/`UNLOCK`, and the
`.terraform.lock.hcl` upload that feeds provider discovery.

tags.name: State Management
tags.description:
The human/UI surface over stored state: workspaces, version history, findings, locks,
the dependency graph, promote/restore and the Resource Inspector.

tags.name: Plans
tags.description:
Redacted `terraform show -json` ingest and the review surface over it. Plan VALUES are
stripped server-side at ingest and never stored or returned.

tags.name: Providers — Management

Per-org provider catalog: what the org serves, from which upstream, under what constraint,
and the scan/verification state of each version.

tags.name: Provider Builds

Self-built and CVE-auto-patched providers: triggering builds, gate overrides, yanking,
policy attestation and the live build-flow view.

tags.name: Policies

Custom Rego policies, per-artefact enablement/enforcement toggles and per-instance

Scanner ingest. **Not part of the public API** — authenticated as the scanner service

tags.name: Internal — Build Pipeline

tags.name: Internal — Policy Bundle

OPA bundle discovery and download. **Not part of the public API** — pulled by the OPA gate

tags.name: Internal — Platform Operator
tags.description:
The platform operator console (`/api/platform/*`). **Not part of the public API.** Every
route is cross-tenant and admits only a platform operator: a human whose portal-SPA token
carries the `platform-operator` role AND whose subject is on the operator allowlist. Every
mutating request, and every denied attempt by a token carrying the role, is written to the
platform audit log.

bearerAuth.description:
An OIDC access token in `Authorization: Bearer`. Three kinds validate here, and the Worker
routes validation by the token's `iss`:

- **Human** — authorization-code + PKCE against the portal application. Carries `email`,
  so RBAC resolves org membership from it.
- **Machine** — `client_credentials` against a confidential application (CI, scanners,
  automation). No `email`, so it is treated as a bot: capped at `member`, and refused
  outright on human-only actions.
- **VCS** — a native GitHub Actions / GitLab CI token, resolved against the org's VCS trust
  entries instead of a client registration (see `vcsOidc`).

Every token must carry the registry audience; request the `terramantle` scope to get it.

basicAuth.description:
HTTP Basic, where the **password half carries the token** and the username is ignored.
Terraform's `http` state backend has no bearer option, so the state and plan surfaces
accept the same credentials this way. Equivalent to `bearerAuth` in every other respect.

oidcPortal.description:
The human portal's OIDC application. `GET /.well-known/terramantle-portal.json` returns
this URL for the deployment being called, which is the value to trust — the literal above
is the production default and is rewritten on the spec served from `GET /openapi.json`.

oauth2Portal.description:
The same portal application expressed as an OAuth2 authorization-code + PKCE flow, so the
interactive docs at `GET /docs` can obtain a real token and call the API as the signed-in
human. The client is public and holds no secret; PKCE is mandatory. Its redirect URI
(`{origin}/docs/oauth2-redirect`) is registered on the application in the IdP.

scopes.email: Email — what RBAC resolves org membership from.
scopes.terramantle: Stamps the registry `aud` and the `roles` claim. Without it the Worker rejects the token.

vcsOidc.description:
A GitHub Actions or GitLab CI OIDC token, presented as a bearer (or in the Basic password
half). No client registration: the Worker validates the token against the issuer, checks
`aud` equals the configured VCS audience, then matches `sub` against the org's VCS trust
entries (`/api/orgs/{orgId}/vcs-trust`). The matched entry decides the org.

A `sub` trusted by more than one org resolves to the **most specific** matching pattern;
anything ambiguous fails closed with `401`. These identities are bots: capped at `member`
and refused on human-only actions.

archiveSignature.name: sig
archiveSignature.description:
An HMAC capability URL, not a credential the caller holds. `terraform`/`tofu` do not
forward `Authorization` when following a download URL, so the Worker mints short-lived
signed URLs for archives and provider files. Entitlement was checked when the URL was
minted; the serve path re-checks blocks and yanks before returning bytes, so a URL minted
before a block does not still resolve to data.

scannerSecret.description:
**Internal.** Either the scanner's OIDC service identity (the only accepted `azp` is the
configured scanner client) or, as a fallback during the OIDC migration, the static
`SCANNER_SECRET` bearer. Fails closed when the scanner client id is unconfigured.

argoResultsSecret.description:
**Internal.** The `ARGO_RESULTS_SECRET` bearer presented by the in-cluster Argo build
Workflow and the queue supervisor. These routes also accept `scannerSecret`.

opaGateOidc.description:
**Internal.** An Authentik `client_credentials` token carrying the `opa-gate` scope, minted
by the OPA gate service. Scope-based rather than role-based on purpose: this is the only
caller that reads every tenant's policy bundle.

webhookSecret.name: X-Webhook-Secret
webhookSecret.description: Shared secret for R2 event notifications, compared in constant time.

stripeSignature.name: Stripe-Signature
stripeSignature.description: Stripe's webhook signature, verified in the handler. No other auth applies.

OrgId.name: orgId
OrgId.description: Org UUID **or** slug. Both are accepted everywhere `orgId` appears.

Workspace.name: workspace
Workspace.description:
State workspace name — a single path segment on the management API. Workspaces whose key
contains slashes on the protocol router appear here with those slashes percent-encoded.

Namespace.name: namespace
Namespace.description:
For modules, the owning org's slug. For providers, the upstream provider namespace
(e.g. `hashicorp`).

Upstream.name: upstream
Upstream.description:
Which lineage of this provider the org manages. An org can manage the same
`namespace/type` from both registries independently; the client's `User-Agent` picks
between them when serving.

ProviderVersion.name: version
ProviderVersion.description:
Provider version. A self-built artifact is always a revision of an upstream base,
`<base>-0.0.<rev>` (e.g. `6.3.3-0.0.2`).

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Clamped to the endpoint's documented maximum.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Caller-generated key that makes this mutation replay-safe. Required: a retry of a state
mutation must not apply twice. A repeat with the same key returns the first outcome with
`idempotent_replay: true`.

ScanVersionId.name: versionId
ScanVersionId.description: Version row id. Resolved across every tenant — see this file's auth note.

UserId.name: userId
UserId.description: `users.id` — the internal UUID, not the OIDC subject.

PlatformAuditCursor.name: cursor
PlatformAuditCursor.description: The previous page's `next_cursor`, verbatim. Opaque; `400` if it was not issued by this endpoint.

PlatformAuditLimit.name: limit
PlatformAuditLimit.description: Rows per page. Values above 200 are clamped to 200.

PlatformIdentityLimit.name: limit
PlatformIdentityLimit.description: Page size. A value outside 1-200 is a `400`, not clamped.

PlatformIdentityCursor.name: cursor
PlatformIdentityCursor.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page. A cursor this API did not issue is a `400`.

PlatformGlobalTokenId.name: id
PlatformGlobalTokenId.description: The `machine_clients.id` of a global token, as `/tokens?scope=global` returns it.

PlatformOperationId.name: id
PlatformOperationId.description: The operation's id, from a plan response.

PlatformProvidersLimit.name: limit
PlatformProvidersLimit.description: Page size, capped at 200. Defaults to 50.

PlatformTenantsUsageDays.name: days
PlatformTenantsUsageDays.description: Window length in UTC days. Only these three windows exist, so a typo is a `400`, not a silently different chart.

RemovedPath.name: path
RemovedPath.description: Any sub-path. Matched as a wildcard; every method answers `410`.

ModuleNamespace.name: namespace
ModuleNamespace.description: Owning org's slug. For modules the namespace **is** the org.

ModuleProvider.name: provider
ModuleProvider.description:
Target provider, per the registry protocol's `namespace/name/provider` triple. Part of the
module's identity, not a reference to a provider artefact.

ProviderOrgSlug.name: orgSlug
ProviderOrgSlug.description:
Org slug whose registry answers. Membership is enforced per request — the slug is never
itself an authorization.

ProviderOs.name: os
ProviderOs.description: Target OS, as Terraform names it.

ProviderArch.name: arch
ProviderArch.description: Target architecture, as Terraform names it.

ProviderFileUpstream.name: upstream
ProviderFileUpstream.description:
Mirrored lineage this file belongs to. The `self_built` sentinel is invalid here — use the
`self_built/{lineage}` path family, which carries the lineage segment the object key needs.

ProviderLineage.name: lineage
ProviderLineage.description:
For a self-built artifact, the registry its source tree came from. Part of the object key:
the same provider built from both registries produces two independent artifacts.

ProviderFilename.name: filename
ProviderFilename.description: Zip filename exactly as named in `SHA256SUMS`.

ArchiveSig.name: sig
ArchiveSig.description:
HMAC signature from the download document. Present ⇒ the signature is the authorization and
no `Authorization` header is read. Absent ⇒ a token is required.

StateKey.name: key
StateKey.description:
Workspace key. The protocol router matches a **wildcard**, so this may contain slashes
(`prod/backend`) — which OpenAPI path templating cannot express. Treat the template as
"the rest of the path".

BadRequest.description: Malformed request — bad JSON, a missing required field, or an unparseable value.

example.message: `action` must be "block", "allow" or null

Unauthorized.description: No credential was presented, or the one presented failed validation.

Forbidden.description:
Authenticated, but not allowed: insufficient role, not a member of this org, a machine
token on a human-only action, or a blocked artefact.

value.message: This action must be performed by a human user

NotFound.description:
No such resource. Also returned when a feature kill-switch is off, and when an artefact is
deliberately hidden rather than refused (`serve_mode: block`).

example.message: Workspace not found

Conflict.description: The request lost a race, or duplicates something that already exists.

example.message: A concurrent build claimed this revision; please retry
Invalid tier

QuotaExceeded.description:
A tier limit was reached. This is an expected business outcome rather than a failure: the
body names the limit, what was counted, and the tier that would raise it.

example.message: State file exceeds 100MB limit

Gone.description: This endpoint was removed. The body names its replacement.

example.message: This endpoint was removed. Provider serving, builds and governance live under /api/orgs/:orgId/providers.

InternalError.description: Unhandled server error. The `req_id` in the Worker log correlates to the trace.

example.message: An unexpected error occurred

NotEnabled.description:
The feature is disabled by a deploy-time switch, or a binding/credential it needs is
unconfigured.

example.message: Self-built providers are not enabled

UpstreamFailed.description: A dependency the Worker fronts failed — the upstream registry, or a queue send.

example.message: Scan could not be queued; please retry

PlatformBacklogBadRequest.description:
A malformed submission: a bad `namespace`, `type` or `version`, a revision passed where a
base was required, or an unparseable body. `message` names which.

PlatformTokenIdpUnavailable.description:
The identity provider refused the lifecycle call. One code for all three verbs; `message`
says which. The Worker's own state is unchanged, so the action can be retried.

example.message: Identity provider rejected token creation

PlatformPolicyDownloadsGzip.description: A gzipped tar, as an attachment.

X-Bundle-Revision.description: The bundle's revision, on bundle downloads.

PlatformPolicyDownloadsJson.description: A JSON document, as an attachment.

PlatformTelemetryNotConfigured.description:
`GRAFANA_API_URL` or `GRAFANA_API_TOKEN` is unset on the worker, so the telemetry surface is
dark. Distinct from a 502: nothing was asked of Grafana.

PlatformTelemetryUpstreamError.description:
Grafana answered, and not with a 2xx. `reason` is `http_<status>`; a 403 there means the
Viewer SA was denied the path rather than that the request was malformed.

PlatformTelemetryUnreachable.description: Grafana did not answer inside the 8s budget. `reason` is `unreachable`.

example.message: This action requires a platform operator

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
The platform's error body. `error` is a stable machine code — branch on it. `message` is
for humans and may change at any time.

allOf.description: An `Error` that also names the fields at fault.

missing.description: Fields that were required and absent or unusable.

RegistryErrors.title: RegistryErrors
RegistryErrors.description:
The Terraform Registry Protocol's error envelope. Used **only** on `/v1/*` routes, because
`terraform`/`tofu` surface `detail` to the operator verbatim — which is how a policy block
explains itself at the point of failure.

errors.title: Module blocked by policy
errors.detail: This module version is not consumable. Failed policies: no-public-ingress

QuotaExceeded.title: QuotaExceeded
QuotaExceeded.description:
Returned with `402`. A tier limit is a business outcome, not an application error — it is
recorded as such in telemetry and never pages anyone.

current.description: Count at the time of the refusal.

max.description: Ceiling on the org's current tier.

upgrade_tier.description: Lowest tier that would allow the request.

Ok.title: Ok
Ok.description: Minimal acknowledgement for an action with nothing to return.

Role.title: Role
Role.description:
Org role, ranked `reader` < `member` < `admin` < `owner`. A guard states a minimum, so a
higher role always passes. Machine identities never exceed `member` whatever this says.

Tier.title: Tier
Tier.description: Billing tier. Drives every quota in `QuotaExceeded`.

UpstreamRegistry.title: UpstreamRegistry
UpstreamRegistry.description:
A public provider registry Terramantle mirrors from. The client's `User-Agent` decides
which lineage an org serves when it manages both (`OpenTofu/` ⇒ `opentofu.org`).

ProviderUpstream.title: ProviderUpstream
ProviderUpstream.description:
`UpstreamRegistry`, plus the `self_built` sentinel for artifacts Terramantle compiled and
signed itself. A self-built row also records the registry lineage its source came from.

ServeMode.title: ServeMode
ServeMode.description:
Whether an org's registry answers for this provider.

- `off` — managed and scanned, but not served. `403` on the version list.
- `serve` — served, subject to the policy gate and per-version blocks.
- `block` — hidden. The version list `404`s so the provider does not advertise that it
  exists at all.

ServeOverride.title: ServeOverride

PolicyArtefactType.title: PolicyArtefactType
PolicyArtefactType.description: The artefact kinds a policy can be written against.

ActorType.title: ActorType
ActorType.description:
How the acting identity authenticated. Display and audit only — never an input to an
authorization decision.

The values are what `deriveActor` writes (`lib/vcsProvenance.ts`), and nothing else is
ever stored:

- `human` — an interactive user token, named by `name`, else `email`, else `sub`.
- `bot_token` — a machine `client_credentials` token, named by its `azp`.
- `vcs` — a native GitHub/GitLab OIDC token presented by CI, named by its `sub`.

This schema previously read `[user, machine, oidc]`, which no code path has ever
produced. It went unnoticed because the field is only ever read for display and every
client modelled it as a free string; a client that generates a closed enum from this
schema rejects every real response instead.

Timestamp.title: Timestamp
Timestamp.description: Epoch milliseconds, matching the D1 column behind it.

OrgGraphNode.title: OrgGraphNode
OrgGraphNode.description:
One node. `kind` discriminates which optional fields are populated; the status fields are
present on every kind so one colour scale covers the whole graph.

id.description:
`ws:<workspace_id>`, `mod:<namespace>/<name>/<provider>` or `prov:<namespace>/<type>`.
The prefix is part of the id, so ids are unique across kinds.

label.description: Display name. Not unique — two orgs can hold the same module name.

namespace.description: Empty string on a state node, which has no namespace.

external.description:
Outside this org, so visible but ungovernable from here. Computed server-side
because the client previously inferred it three different ways and disagreed with
itself about whether to offer governance actions.

blocked.description: An admin kill switch, an enforcing policy, or a serve override refuses it.

blocked_reason.description: Whichever mechanism fired. `null` when not blocked, or when none recorded one.

policy_failed.description: The latest published version fails at least one policy. Always false for state and provider nodes.

critical_count.description: From the latest published version. `0` on a stub, a state node, or an unscanned module — a zero here is not a clean bill of health.

outdated.description: Provider nodes only: some workspace pins a version older than the newest satisfying its constraint.

latest_version.description:
Newest PUBLISHED version by publish time, not a lexicographic max — `v10` sorts above
`v9`. `null` when a module has no published version, which includes one still being
scanned and one whose scan failed.

version_count.description: Published versions only, so `0` means nothing consumable exists yet.

discovered.description:
Provider nodes only. `true` when the provider was surfaced by discovery — a lock file
or a module's `required_providers` — rather than added by an admin. A referenced
provider we hold no artefact row for defaults to `true`: being referenced is the
discovery.

has_lock_file.description:
State nodes only. `false` means Terramantle cannot see this workspace's provider
pins, so it cannot warn about CVEs or stale versions for it — the portal offers an
upload prompt on these nodes rather than leaving them as unexplained orphans.

lock_file_uploaded_at.description:
State nodes only. When the workspace's `.terraform.lock.hcl` was last uploaded.
Every `locks` edge leaving this node states the estate as of this moment, so the
portal renders it as the as-of line rather than as a decorative timestamp. Lives on
the node and not on the edges because it is one fact per workspace, not one per pin.

lock_file_uploaded_by.description:
The uploader's email where the recorded value was a user id, otherwise the raw OIDC
client id — a lock file is routinely pushed by CI, so the client id is the honest
answer rather than a missing one.

infrastructure_repo_url.description:
The user's own Terraform repository, recorded from a header at upload time. Not
allowlist-checked server-side, unlike `vcs_commit_url`, so the portal must render it
through its safe-URL guard.

serial.description: Serial of the newest state version.

vcs_commit_url.description:
Pre-built commit link, `https` on an allowlisted host only. Built server-side on
purpose: a forged VCS claim must not be able to steer a link the portal renders.
`null` whenever provenance is absent — which is the common case, since it is recorded
only for pushes authenticated by VCS OIDC, not for human or bot-token pushes.

OrgGraphEdge.title: OrgGraphEdge
OrgGraphEdge.description:
A relationship and the facts that belong to it rather than to either endpoint: the
version a workspace pinned, the constraint a module declared, and the release that
declared it. Fields beyond the four required ones are present only for the relations
named in their descriptions, so read `rel` first.

Deliberately absent: the lock file's `hashes`. At 5-15 entries of ~55 characters that is
300-800 bytes on every `locks` edge, which would add roughly a megabyte to a large org's
graph for a value nothing renders. The hash set is on the workspace's Providers tab.

from.description: Node id of the consumer. Edges point consumer → dependency.

rel.description:
`depends` module → module, `requires` module → provider (`required_providers`),
`locks` state → provider (a lock-file pin). Module-sourced edges are scoped to the
module's latest published version, so a dependency dropped in a later release stops
being drawn.

constraint.description:
The declared version constraint, where one was recorded. `null` carries meaning and
differs by relation: on `requires` it is a `required_providers` block with no
`version`, i.e. **any version**; on `locks` it is a lock file that recorded no
constraint. Neither is a missing value, and the portal words them differently.

declared_in_version.description:
`depends` and `requires`. The version of the CONSUMER module whose source declares
this relationship. On the org graph that is always the module's latest published
version, since module-sourced edges are scoped to it; on the version-scoped module
graph it is the version in the path.

is_terramantle.description:
`depends` only. The dependency resolves inside this Terramantle registry rather than
an external source. Recorded at scan time from the source address.

upstream.description:
`requires` and `locks`. Which registry the relationship names. This is the only place
a registry appears, because provider NODES deliberately collapse the two — an org may
hold `hashicorp/local` from both, while `module_provider_refs.upstream` is nullable
and so a module ref cannot always be attributed to one. `null` on a `requires` edge
therefore means "not recorded", not "neither".

locked_version.description:
`locks` only. The version the lock file actually pins — the fact the graph exists to
surface. Compare against `latest_matching` for staleness; the node-level `outdated`
flag is an OR across every workspace pinning the provider and so cannot say which
pin is behind.

provider_address.description:
`locks` only. The literal address in the lock file, e.g.
`registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws`. Also what distinguishes two parallel edges
when one workspace pins the same provider from both registries.

locked_at.description: `locks` only. When the pin was recorded.

latest_matching.description:
`locks` only. Newest version satisfying `constraint`. `null` is ambiguous on its own
and must be read with the two timestamps below: it means "nothing newer satisfies the
constraint" only when `latest_version_checked_at` is set.

latest_version.description:
`locks` only. Newest version upstream, IGNORING the constraint. A different question
from `latest_matching`, and presenting the two as one is how a pin that is correctly
held back by its own constraint gets reported as stale.

latest_version_checked_at.description:
`locks` only. When the version checker last SUCCEEDED for this pin. `null` with
`latest_lookup_error_at` set means the pin has never been compared against the
registry, which is a different state from "up to date" and is rendered as such.

latest_lookup_error_at.description: `locks` only. When an upstream lookup last failed.

modules.v1.description: Base path of the module registry protocol.

providers.v1.description:
Base path of the provider registry protocol. Org-scoped on an org subdomain, bare
otherwise.

ApiSpecLinks.title: ApiSpecLinks
ApiSpecLinks.description:
Where this deployment's machine-readable contract lives. Advertised for the same reason the
issuer is: a client should never have to be told, and the served documents have this
deployment's origin and issuer substituted in, which a committed copy cannot.

docs_redirect_uri.description:
The redirect URI `/docs` runs its PKCE flow against. Published so an operator can diff
it against the application's registered redirect URIs instead of guessing why sign-in
fails — a missing entry there is that flow's one failure mode.

api_url.description: Origin this document was served from — what the CLI should call.

issuer.description: Per-application OIDC issuer for the CLI's own client.

discovery_url.description: RFC 8414 metadata URL; the CLI resolves the device + token endpoints from it.

audience.description: Registry audience every user/CI token must carry.

vcs_audience.description:
Audience GitHub/GitLab CI must mint its OIDC token for. Falls back to `audience`
when no distinct VCS audience is configured.

device_client_id.description:
Public client for the device-authorization flow, or `null` until provisioned — in
which case the CLI reports a clear error rather than attempting a login.

bot_client_id.description:
Confidential provider every bot token authenticates against, or `null` when the
deployment has not provisioned one.

There is no per-bot client. A bot token created in the portal is an IdP service
account under this single provider, so the `client_credentials` grant sends
`client_id` = this value, `username` = the token's Client ID and `password` =
its Client Secret — not the client_id/client_secret pair the grant name suggests.
Advertised here so the CLI does not compile in a deployment-specific name.

scopes.description:
Space-separated scopes to request. `terramantle` is load-bearing: it stamps the
registry `aud` and the `roles` claim, and without it the Worker rejects the bearer.

client_id.description: Public PKCE client id, or `null` until provisioned.

FindingCategory.description:
Tool-agnostic finding category. The underlying scanner tool that produced
the finding is internal-only and is never surfaced in public API responses.

PublicModuleFinding.description: A finding attached to a module version, as returned by the registry API. The `tool` property is stripped at the API boundary and never exposed publicly.

rule_id.description: Scanner rule or check identifier, if available.

file_path.description: Path of the file in which the finding was detected, relative to the module root.

line_start.description: First line of the affected range (1-indexed).

line_end.description: Last line of the affected range (1-indexed, inclusive).

resource.description: Terraform resource address or identifier related to the finding.

meta.description: Free-form tool-specific metadata. Shape varies by category and rule.

PublicStateFinding.description: A finding derived from a Terraform state file, as returned by the GET /api/v1/{orgId}/state/{workspace}/findings endpoint. The `tool` property is stripped at the API boundary. There are no file_path or line_start/line_end fields (state files carry no source location).

rule_id.description: Scanner rule or check identifier, if available.

resource.description: Terraform resource address or identifier related to the finding.

meta.description:
Free-form metadata. For exposure findings, meta carries a `subtype`
discriminator string with one of the following values:
  - 'endpoint' — an exposed HTTP/HTTPS endpoint
  - 'port'     — an exposed network port

All other fields in meta are tool-specific and should not be relied
upon as stable contract.

InternalModuleFindingInput.description: A finding item within the scanner -> worker POST /internal/scan-results payload. Extends PublicModuleFinding with a required `tool` field and an optional `category` (the worker derives category from tool+rule_id when absent, during rollout).

tool.description: The scanner tool that produced this finding.

category.description:
Tool-agnostic category. Optional during rollout — the worker will
derive it from the tool and rule_id if absent. Once all scanners
populate this field it will become required.

InternalStateFindingInput.description: A finding item within the scanner -> worker POST /internal/scan-results/state payload. Extends PublicStateFinding with a required `tool` field and an optional `category` (same rollout semantics as InternalModuleFindingInput).

tool.description: The scanner tool that produced this finding.

category.description:
Tool-agnostic category. Optional during rollout — the worker derives
it from the tool and rule_id if absent.

meta.description:
Free-form metadata. For exposure findings, meta carries a `subtype`
discriminator string ('endpoint' | 'port').

PresignedUrl.title: PresignedUrl
PresignedUrl.description:
A short-lived presigned object-storage URL. The scan pod is untrusted and holds no bucket
credentials — this URL is the entire grant.

key.description: The object key the URL addresses.

ScanClaimResult.title: ScanClaimResult
ScanClaimResult.description:
Read both booleans. `claimed: false, proceed: true` is the interesting case: a previous
attempt may have died mid-run, and re-scanning is safe because ingest is a race-safe
upsert.

status.description: The job's current status, when the claim did not succeed.

ScanPolicyResultInput.title: ScanPolicyResultInput
ScanPolicyResultInput.description: One OPA verdict as a scanner reports it.

ModuleDependencyInput.title: ModuleDependencyInput
ModuleDependencyInput.description: One module-to-module dependency edge parsed from the source.

is_terramantle.description: Whether the dependency resolves inside this registry.

RequiredProviderRef.title: RequiredProviderRef
RequiredProviderRef.description:
One `required_providers` entry parsed from a module's source. This is how a provider becomes
a **discovered** artefact in the consuming org's catalog.

version_constraint.description: The constraint as written, or `null` when the source omitted one.

status.description: `failed` means the SCAN failed — distinct from a policy block.

required_providers.description: Drives provider discovery. Additive — an older scanner omits it.

StateScanResultsBody.title: StateScanResultsBody
StateScanResultsBody.description: Findings must carry metadata only — never a secret value.

policy_results.description:
A failing **enforcing** verdict sets the workspace block that the next apply's `LOCK` is
refused on. Stored whether or not policies are enabled, so re-enabling re-blocks.

real_resource_count.description:
Best-effort. Absent (older scanner) or `null` (classifier bailout) leaves the stored
columns untouched — which is also how pre-classification versions get backfilled.

providers.description:
The providers backing this state's **managed** resources, parsed from each resource's
provider address. Feeds provider discovery, so each one becomes a discovered artefact
for the org and gets scanned.

This is the second of two discovery sources, and the one that reaches most orgs. The
first is an uploaded `.terraform.lock.hcl`, which carries pinned versions but which
few workspaces ever upload — so without this, the providers of every workspace
without a lock file never became artefacts at all and were invisible to CVE and
outdated-version reporting.

Carries no version on purpose: state records *which* provider is in use, never which
version. Where a lock file names the same provider, its pinned constraint wins.

Optional and additive, so a scanner can ship ahead of the Worker; absent is a no-op.

StateProviderInput.title: StateProviderInput
StateProviderInput.description: One provider observed in a state file's managed resources.

namespace.description: The namespace segment of the provider address, e.g. `hashicorp`.

upstream.description:
Derived from the address host, matching how lock-file and module discovery resolve it:
an explicit `registry.opentofu.org` means `opentofu.org`, anything else defaults to
`terraform.io`.

category.description: Derived by the Worker from `tool` and `rule_id` when absent.

ProviderScanResultsBody.title: ProviderScanResultsBody
ProviderScanResultsBody.description:
One per scanned version. A job emits several; they attach to the job by `job_id`, which is
what makes the attachment race-safe when two jobs for one provider overlap.

org_id.description: `null` on a platform-scoped scan — an auto-patch patched-tree scan has no requesting org.

provider_type.description: Named `provider_type` rather than `type` to avoid the JavaScript collision.

job_failed.description:
A job-level terminal failure — for example a constraint that matched no versions. Marks
the whole job failed; the per-version fields are absent.

error_message.description: Job-level reason, or this version's reason on a `failed`/`skipped` report.

matched_count.description: Versions matching the constraint before the per-job cap. Constant across a job's reports.

status.description:
`published` ⇒ scanned. `failed` ⇒ attempted and failed (enters the retry tier).
`skipped` ⇒ **never attempted** because the job ran out of wall budget: no result row is
written and the backlog marker is re-armed for the next drain.

source_commit_sha.description: Exact upstream commit the version tag pointed at when scanned — source provenance.

clamav_unscanned.description:
Archives the malware scan left out because a member inflates past clamd's per-file limit
(512 MiB), so ClamAV could not have scanned all of it. A **coverage gap, not a
detection**: `malware_detected` is unaffected. Stored as JSON on the shared row; omitted
or empty when nothing was left out. Older scanners never send it.

member.description: The archive member that exceeded the limit; `null` for a single-file `.gz`.

scan_started_at.description: Scan start, epoch milliseconds. Duration is `scanned_at - scan_started_at`.

source_signals.description: Supply-chain trust signals from the source repository. Self-built only.

policy_results.description:
Self-built only. Materialised per-org, with the blocked gate derived from each policy's
enforcing flag.

BuildPlatformResult.title: BuildPlatformResult
BuildPlatformResult.description:
One platform the build produced. A platform that failed to compile is **excluded** rather
than reported as failed — publish-what-built.

PatchProvenanceInput.title: PatchProvenanceInput
PatchProvenanceInput.description:
On success, the git provenance of a patched build. On a failure report, the stage and
reason instead — which is what the UI and the auto-patch scheduler read to decide whether
to retry.

source_tree_hash.description:
Structural digest of the pinned source tree. The gate verdicts bind to this value —
it is what makes "the bytes scanned are the bytes built" checkable.

status.description: Present only from the failure reporter; absent means a successful publish.

attempt.description:
Which queue DELIVERY this workflow ran for (`0` = first). **The retry discriminator**: a
higher attempt than the stored row's re-opens a terminal row; equal-or-lower is a
duplicate and is ignored.

source_upstream.description:
The registry lineage the artifacts were published under. **Required on success** and
must equal the job row's lineage — it is part of the object key, so a mismatch is
refused rather than published somewhere nothing will look.

attempt.description: Retry attempt; `0` for the first run.

message.description: Node failure message, capped by the producer.

msg_key.description: The claim key — a build/scan job id, or a version id for module/state/plan scans.

workflow_name.description: `null` while the claim exists but no workflow has been observed yet.

phase.description: `null` when no workflow exists for the claim.

message.description: Workflow status message. Gate markers land here.

attempt.description: Queue delivery attempt of the lease this claim holds.

observed_at.description:
Supervisor clock when this state was observed. **The ordering guard** — the Worker drops
an event older than the stored timestamp, so a slow tick cannot overwrite newer state.

patch_failure.description: Structured patch failure, read from the patch node's output parameter.

settle.description: Present only on the tick that settled the queue message.

heartbeat.description:
Sent **every tick, even with zero claims**. Its absence is how the reapers tell a lost
workflow from a supervisor that is down.

at_capacity.description:
The pull loop is paused at its claim ceiling, so an unleased message may be
legitimate queued work — absence-based reaping must pause too.

list_ok.description:
`false` ⇒ this tick's cluster list failed. Claims cannot settle, but the lease side
is still alive, which is what the lost-message arm cares about.

BacklogProviderRef.title: BacklogProviderRef
BacklogProviderRef.description: How operator tooling names a provider version. The owning org is resolved server-side.

version.description: For a build, the upstream base (`X.Y.Z`) — never a revision.

id.description:
The internal user id. This, not the OIDC subject, is the identity other endpoints take
as `userId`.

slug.description:
URL-safe identity. Accepted anywhere `orgId` appears, and it is the `namespace` segment
for this org's modules.

claimed_domain.description: Email domain whose new sign-ups join this org automatically.

is_personal.description: A personal org is the user's own account. Always reports `starter`.

is_billing_admin.description: Grants billing access without promoting the member to `admin`.

last_seen_at.description:
Last authenticated request by this user, anywhere on the platform — not a login
event. The auth middleware writes it at most once per five minutes per identity
(same throttle as `MachineTokenSummary.last_used_at`), so read it as "recently
seen", and note that a still-valid session or a CLI call counts as activity
without anyone signing in again.

`null` means never seen — for an invited member that means they have not been
back since the login that created their user record, because
`POST /api/orgs/{orgId}/members` can only invite someone who has logged in at
least once.

Informational only: it exists so an owner can tell a live seat from a dormant
one. No authorization decision reads it, and it is not scoped to this org.

NotificationCadence.title: NotificationCadence
NotificationCadence.description: How often the org wants provider-update notifications.

subject.description: Pattern matched against the CI token's `sub`.

TokenScope.title: TokenScope
TokenScope.description:
What a machine token can reach.

- `global` — **every** org on the platform (write on modules), not just the orgs its creator
  administers. Creatable only by a platform operator; still listed here because existing
  global tokens appear in token listings.
- `org` — one org, with per-domain read/write via `include_modules` / `include_state`.
- `state_workspaces` — one org, but state only on the workspaces in `state_grants`.

StateTokenGrant.title: StateTokenGrant
StateTokenGrant.description: One workspace a `state_workspaces`-scoped token may touch, and how.

state_grants.description: Required in substance for `state_workspaces` scope — without grants the token reaches no state.

examples.name: prod-apply
examples.description: GitHub Actions apply job for prod

MachineTokenSummary.title: MachineTokenSummary
MachineTokenSummary.description:
A machine identity's metadata. Never carries a secret.

`last_used_at` and the geo fields are written at most once per five minutes per identity —
the auth middleware runs on every request and rewriting the row each time would churn it
for data nobody needs at sub-minute resolution. Read them as "recently seen".

oidc_client_id.description: The token's `azp`. This is the identity the API authorizes.

client_secret.description:
**Returned once, here.** Never stored and never retrievable again — a lost secret
means rotating the token.

TierFeatureFlags.title: TierFeatureFlags
TierFeatureFlags.description:
What the org's tier allows. A `false` flag is why an otherwise-valid request answers `402`
with `QuotaExceeded`.

providerServe.description: Whether the org's registry may answer provider requests at all.

usage.description: Current counts against the counted limits.

active.description: Whether the window is still open.

grace_period.description: `null` when no downgrade grace period is set.

has_stripe.description: Whether a Stripe subscription backs this org.

AuditAction.title: AuditAction
AuditAction.description: The governance actions recorded in the audit log.

actor_user_id.description: `null` for a platform-initiated action with no human actor.

metadata.description:
A **JSON string**, not an object — stored verbatim as written. Shape varies by
`action`; parse it per action rather than treating it as a stable contract.

DailyPoint.title: DailyPoint
DailyPoint.description: One UTC day. Series are sparse — days with no activity are omitted.

TenantAnalytics.title: TenantAnalytics
TenantAnalytics.description:
The org dashboard's payload. Rollup counts and series only — no resource values and no
state or plan contents.

Every series is **sparse**: days with no activity are omitted and the client zero-fills.
Totals and 30-day counts cover downloads; the per-module and per-workspace series cover 90
days.

top_module_download_series.description: Top 5 modules by downloads over 90 days, each with its daily series.

top_workspace_push_series.description: Top 5 workspaces by pushes over 90 days, each with its daily series.

patch_adoption.description: Continuous-patching exposure: vulnerable superseded versions still being downloaded.

module_findings_artifacts.description: Per-severity drill-down for the open-findings donuts.

OrgGraphStats.title: OrgGraphStats
OrgGraphStats.description: Coverage totals for the org, used to explain what the graph is NOT showing.

total.description: Modules in the org. External stub nodes are never counted.

scanned.description: Modules with at least one scan-completed published version.

unscanned_no_versions.description: Modules with no published version: mid-scan, scan failed, or pruned.

workspaces_without_lock_file.description: Workspaces whose provider pins are invisible to Terramantle.

PlanVersionSummary.description: Client-facing plan version summary (list + detail). Action counts derive from `resource_changes[].change.actions`; a replace (delete+create) counts ONCE under `replace_count`, not under add/destroy. No workspace_id / storage internals leak.

sensitive_change_count.description: Changes touching a sensitive attribute (count only, never the value).

attestation_hash.description: sha-256 of the redacted canonical plan JSON.

prior_serial.description: Prior state serial the plan was made against (from X-Plan-Prior-Serial).

PublicPlanFinding.description: A redacted finding attached to a plan version. The `tool` property is stripped at the API boundary (kept internal, mirrors PublicStateFinding). Plan findings carry an `attr` (the attribute that forces a replacement / carries the finding). No concrete value appears in any field.

description.description: Attribute path / metadata — never a concrete value.

attr.description: The attribute that forces replacement / carries the finding.

meta.description: Free-form metadata (e.g. `meta.provider` for a replacement). Value-free.

PlanPolicyResult.description: One persisted plan policy-evaluation result. `source` discriminates the synchronous built-in M2 gate (`builtin`, policy_id null) from the async advisory OPA pass (`opa`). Redacted-safe: `failure_msg` carries gate reasons only.

policy_id.description: Null for the built-in gate (no policies row).

failure_msg.description: Joined gate reasons when not passed; null when passed.

PlanAttestation.description: Apply-matches-review verdict for a (workspace, attestation_hash). `attested` = a plan_version with this hash was ingested/redacted here; `approved` = an active override binds a human review to this hash; `stale` = the plan's prior_serial trails the workspace's current state serial. FAIL-CLOSED: a CI gate MUST require `attested && approved && !stale`.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of the verdict (states the fail-closed rule).

ReplacementByProvider.description: Cross-workspace forced-replacement rollup for one provider (M5). `workspaces` is where this provider forces a delete+create in a recent plan; `blast_radius_ workspace_count` is how many workspaces use the provider at all.

provider.description: Provider label (meta.provider, else resource type prefix, else "unknown").

GateConfig.description: The built-in M2 gate configuration for a scope (org default when workspace-less; a per-workspace override otherwise — per-workspace wins). `destroy_denylist` is a JSON array of resource types. No config at all = an all-clear gate (never blocks).

max_destroys.description: Block if the plan's destroy count (incl. replace-halves) exceeds this. Null = no cap.

destroy_denylist.description: Block if any destroyed resource type is in this list (incl. replace-halves).

require_approval.description: Hold every plan pending manual approval when true.

PlanScanResultsBody.description: The plan-scanner -> worker POST /internal/scan-results/plan payload. Findings are metadata-only. `policy_results` are ADVISORY OPA verdicts (stored source='opa'); the enforcing built-in gate row is written inline at ingest and is never erased by a rescan.

PlanFindingInput.description: A finding item in the plan scan-results payload. Metadata only — `description`, `resource`, and `attr` are addresses/paths, NEVER a concrete value.

tool.description: Scanner tool that produced the finding (kept internal; not surfaced publicly).

category.description: Plan category (drift / replacement / secret_exposure / stateful_destroy). Free text.

PlanPolicyResultInput.description: An advisory OPA policy verdict in the plan scan-results payload. Upserted on UNIQUE(plan_version_id, policy_id) with source='opa'; never collides with the built-in (policy_id null) row.

version.description:
For `build` and `reopen-build`, the upstream BASE (`X.Y.Z`). For `rescan`, either a base
or a `<base>-0.0.N` revision of ours.

upstream.description: Picks the lineage when an org holds both. Omitted, it is resolved the way the drain resolves it.

org_id.description: The tenant a completed build is entitled to. Omitted means platform-initiated.

dispatch.description:
`return` does all the same work and hands the queue message back instead of sending it,
for a runner that executes the job itself.

result.description: The task's own accounting, shape depending on the task.

reason.description: Required. Recorded in the audit event.

granted.description: True when this call created the row (POST only).

already_held.description: True when the row was already there (POST only).

revoked.description: True when a row was removed (DELETE only).

tenant_slug.description: `null` only if the tenant row is gone (it is referenced by FK, so this should not happen).

actor_user_id.description: `null` for bot and system actions, which have no users row.

metadata.description: The stored JSON, parsed. A value that is not valid JSON comes back as its raw string. `null` when none.

beyond_tenant_retention.description: Older than the org's tier retention - still stored, but no longer on the org's own audit page.

actor_sub.description: The token subject (an email for portal tokens). `(anonymous)` if no user was resolved.

actor_azp.description: The client the token was issued to. A denial with a non-portal `azp` is `wrong_client`.

result.description: ok: done. denied: authz refused. refused: a precondition refused it. error: it failed.

req_id.description: cf-ray; joins the Cloudflare edge logs.

metadata.description: The stored JSON, parsed (for a denial, `{"reason": "..."}`). `null` when none.

last_24h.description: Rows per result in the last 24 hours, over the whole table, ignoring the filters.

kind.description:
A `brake` is something to pull in an incident; a `feature` is a capability switch. The
distinction is for the operator's eye, not the resolver.

semantics.description:
Which rule the call site was written with. `on_when_1`: enabled only when the value is
exactly "1". `off_when_0`: enabled unless the value is exactly "0". Null for a `number`
flag, which has its own parser.

effect.description: What turning it off actually stops, in the words needed mid-incident.

raw.description: The string in force, from whichever layer won.

effective.description: The decision the worker is making now, after the flag's own parsing.

env_value.description: What the deploy says — i.e. what removing an override would revert to.

PlatformFleetStuckArm.title: PlatformFleetStuckArm

thresholds.description: The reaper and observer constants the figures were computed with, in ms.

in_flight.description:
Non-terminal rows per table and status. provider_version_scans splits `pending` into
`pending (awaiting drain)` (no `queued_at`: backlog the drain has not dispatched) and
`pending (dispatched)`.

scan_attempts_24h.description: Module/state/plan scan attempts ENQUEUED in the window. Providers are not in scan_attempts.

error_classes.description: Failed, abandoned and not_queued attempts by `error_class` (top 50). A null class is an attempt that failed without one.

provider_jobs_24h.description: provider_build_jobs and provider_scan_jobs TRIGGERED in the last 24 hours, by status.

present.description: `false` = no heartbeat row has ever been written for this kind.

fresh.description: The beat is no older than `thresholds.heartbeat_max_age_ms`.

inflight.description: Claims the supervisor held at its last beat.

at_capacity.description: The pull loop was paused at its claim ceiling; the lost-message reaper arm stands down.

list_ok.description: The supervisor's last Workflow list against the apiserver succeeded.

source.description: The D1 table the row lives in.

label.description: A human label (provider address and version, module name, workspace name).

since.description: The timestamp the reaper keys this arm on.

tenant_id.description: The requesting or owning org. Null for shared provider markers, and for platform-initiated provider jobs.

PlatformFleetFlowState.title: PlatformFleetFlowState
PlatformFleetFlowState.description: The output of lib/providerFlowState.ts deriveFlowState, from the pushed snapshot only.

observed_at.description: The supervisor's last observation (flow_updated_at); the staleness signal.

name.description:
Shown in both consoles and used to derive the IdP service-account username, so make it
say what holds the token. Trimmed; blank is a `400`. Not unique — the id is.

description.description: Why this token exists. Blank or absent is stored as `null`.

PlatformGlobalTokenCreated.title: PlatformGlobalTokenCreated
PlatformGlobalTokenCreated.description:
The new token. `client_secret` appears here and in a `/rotate` response only — it is not
stored, so this body is the one chance to copy it.

tenant_id.description: Always `null` — a global token belongs to no org.

oidc_client_id.description: The IdP client id (an Authentik service-account username). An identifier, not a secret.

oidc_app_id.description: The IdP application id, which is what revoke and rotate address.

is_global.description: Always `1` here. The column is an integer, not a boolean, as stored.

client_secret.description: Shown exactly once. Not stored by the Worker and not recoverable from the IdP.

deleted_at.description: Unix ms of the soft delete; `null` for a live org.

tenant.description: The owning org; `null` for a global token.

include_modules.description: Module access for an `org` token (`none`/`read`/`write`); `null` for other scopes.

subject.description: Prefix matched against the CI token's `sub` claim, e.g. `repo:owner/*`.

left_at.description: Set when the user soft-left the org; a re-join clears it.

last_seen_at.description: Last authenticated request (5-minute resolution), not a login event.

tier.description: The tier the visitor picked (`Solo`, `Team`, `Business`, `Enterprise`, `Founding member`), if any.

email.description: `null` when the user row is gone (feature_interest.user_id is not a foreign key).

name.description: The `.sql` file name without its extension.

severity.description: `error`: a finding is a live defect that breaks serving, scanning or access. `warn`: worth a look, not urgent.

description.description: The file's `-- why:` header - what breaks when this check returns rows.

fix.description: The file's `-- fix:` header - what to do about a finding.

examples.name: zz_legacy_leftovers
examples.description: rename-aside tables (zz_legacy_*, *_old) left behind by a rebuild migration keep stale data and stale FK targets alive
examples.fix: once the owning migration has soaked, drop them in a follow-up migration (097's deferred 099 pattern)

status.description:
`pass`: no rows. `findings`: one or more rows (read `severity` for how bad).
`error`: the query failed, so the check says nothing either way. `skipped`: the
run's time budget ran out before this check started.

finding_count.description: Rows the query returned. Not a total when `at_limit` is true.

at_limit.description: The query returned as many rows as its own LIMIT, so there may be more findings than `finding_count`.

rows.description: The first rows returned, as the query's columns. Columns differ per check.

error.description: Why the check errored or was skipped; `null` otherwise.

failed.description: Checks of severity `error` that returned rows.

warned.description: Checks of severity `warn` that returned rows.

results.name: zz_legacy_leftovers
results.description: rename-aside tables (zz_legacy_*, *_old) left behind by a rebuild migration keep stale data and stale FK targets alive
results.fix: once the owning migration has soaked, drop them in a follow-up migration (097's deferred 099 pattern)

target.description:
`<namespace>/<type>` for a provider wipe, `*` for a provider purge, and the org's SLUG
for an org purge (the id is in the plan; the slug is what a human can retype).

env.description:
The environment the plan was made against. An apply in a different one is refused, so a
staging plan can never be applied in production.

status.description:
`incomplete` is not a failure: the deletes ran and the re-inventory still found
something. It is resumable, and `result` says what was left.

phase.description: The resume point. For a wipe, the object sweeps run before the row deletes.

attempts.description: Lease claims so far. A number climbing with no phase change means slices are dying.

expires_at.description: When the plan goes stale. Only meaningful while `planned`.

result.description:
What the run did and what it left. For a wipe: the per-phase tally, any prefix still
populated, leftover object failures, rows remaining, the kept-table counts, and the fork
repositories and shared bundles it deliberately left alone. For a purge: the tally and
the exit-check verdicts.

PlatformVolatileDiff.description:
Fields that moved between plan and apply WITHOUT withdrawing consent — download counts, row
counts, object counts. Reported, never blocking: hashing these would mean a provider anyone
uses could never be wiped.

arm_problem.description: Why an apply would be refused, available at plan time so it is not a surprise.

inventory.description:
Row counts per table, the kept-table counts, the cached versions, in-flight work, fork
repositories, the vcs-stats rows owned versus shared, the owned versus shared source
bundles, the explicitly referenced object keys, and the object prefixes. Prefixes always
end in `/` so `aws/` cannot match `aws-x/`.

blast_radius.description: Orgs serving the provider, and who downloaded it in the last seven days.

precondition.description:
Every gate and whether it is satisfied, all evaluated together so a refusal names each
unmet one at once rather than making an operator fix them a 409 at a time.

detail.description: What to change, in operator terms.

failed_24h.description: Jobs that ended `failed` in the last 24 hours.

finished_24h.description: Jobs that left the in-flight set in the last 24 hours, whatever their outcome.

by_tier.description: Active orgs per tier, largest first.

seen_7d.description: Users whose `last_seen_at` is within the last 7 days.

queue_kinds.description: Queue kinds that have ever reported a workflow-observer heartbeat.

oldest.description: The least recent heartbeat, or `null` when no observer has ever reported.

forms_7d.description: Contact/sales form submissions in the last 7 days.

interest_7d.description: Feature-interest clicks in the last 7 days.

computed_revision.description: What the policy rows hash to now; `null` for an org with no policies.

instance_key.description: `null` = org baseline; a value = custom to one module/workspace/provider.

deleted_at.description: Epoch ms of the soft delete; `null` for a live org.

revision.description: The published bundle revision; `null` when `status` is `missing`.

contract_version.description: The policy-input contract the published bundle was built against.

bundle_updated_at.description: Epoch ms the bundle pointer last moved.

generated_at.description: Epoch ms the worker built this report; ages are relative to it.
Epoch ms of the last publish, which only happens when the content changed.

kev_rows.description: CVEs currently flagged as on the CISA KEV catalogue.

kev_swept_at.description: Epoch ms of the last KEV sweep (oldest `updated_at` among KEV rows).

newest_kev_added_at.description: CISA's own `dateAdded` on the newest entry. CISA adds a few a week; weeks old means the mirror is not refreshing.

epss_rows.description: CVEs with an EPSS score at or above the stored floor.

PlatformProvidersRows.title: PlatformProvidersRows
PlatformProvidersRows.description: Aggregate rows exactly as the shared SQL returns them (column names are the contract).

scan_jobs.description: Per status: n, done_1h, done_24h, stale (in flight > 90m), oldest_inflight_ms.

scan_timing.description: Last 24h completed/partial: n, claim_avg_ms, claim_max_ms, run_avg_ms, run_max_ms, versions, findings. Averages are null when n is 0.

scan_failures.description: Top five failure messages (first 90 chars) in the last 24h: error, n, last_ms.

build_jobs.description: Per (status, requested_via): n, done_1h, done_24h, stuck (building > 1h or pending > 3h), oldest_inflight_ms.

build_timing.description: Last 24h completed: n, run_avg_ms, run_max_ms, platforms, gates_passed.

patched.description: patched_provider_versions per (status, failure_stage): n, created_24h, published_24h.

trend.description: Hourly completions, 24 values each, OLDEST FIRST (the last value is the current hour).

inflight_count.description: D1 scan and build jobs not yet terminal.

missing_workflow.description:
In-flight D1 jobs with no live Workflow (first 50). A pending scan job waits for the
drain, so only processing/building rows here are suspicious.

orphan_running.description: Running/Pending provider Workflows whose D1 job is already terminal (first 50).

errors.description: Section name -> query error. Empty when every section loaded.

thresholds_ms.description: The drain's own thresholds the states were derived with.

scan.description: Count per scan state, every state present.

outstanding.description: Versions with actionable work (scan backlog, build-due or build-failed).

providers.description: Per-provider rollup of the filtered set.

orphan.description: No artefact version backs this row (a self_built lineage, or a removed artefact). Still real work.

age_ms.description: scanned_at, else queued_at, as epoch ms (despite the name, a timestamp).

PlatformProvidersFlowState.title: PlatformProvidersFlowState
PlatformProvidersFlowState.description:
lib/providerFlowState.ts deriveFlowState. `unknown` means nothing could vouch for the job
(stale snapshot, no live answer) and is never shown as `queued`. `blocked` is a gate block,
the product working; the reason is in the Workflow CR.

PlatformProvidersArgoRead.title: PlatformProvidersArgoRead
PlatformProvidersArgoRead.description:
What the detail route's Argo read returned. `ok: false` is a failed or skipped read - no
information - with `reason` one of `not_configured`, `no_workflow_uid` (terminal row with
nothing to look up), `unreachable` or `http_<n>`. `ok: true, found: false` is a successful
read that found nothing, which IS evidence.

PlatformProvidersArgoCr.title: PlatformProvidersArgoCr
PlatformProvidersArgoCr.description: Where to read the Workflow CR by hand - the only place a gate block's reason lives.

archive_api_path.description: The Argo server API path for the archived Workflow, when the uid is known.

job.description: The list fields (without `flow`) plus source/bundle hashes, sha256sums and the raw flow columns.

gate_verdicts.description: Empty for a blocked build - see `argo_cr`.

patched_revisions.description: patched_provider_versions rows whose build_job_id is this job.

lineage_upstream.description: For self_built scans, the registry the tree was built from.

PlatformTelemetrySource.description:
Which datasource. The UIDs are pinned in `lib/telemetryQuery.ts` rather than looked up by
name: a name lookup would make the allowlist follow a rename in Grafana, which is the wrong
behaviour for an allowlist. If a datasource is recreated its UID changes and the console
says so instead of quietly querying something else.

from.description: Epoch ms, inclusive — the window actually queried.

capped.description:
True when the requested range was wider than the cap. The window is narrowed by moving
`from` forward, keeping the most recent part.

database.description: Grafana's own view of its database, from `/api/health`.

public_url.description: Browser-facing Grafana, for Explore links. Never called by the worker.

caps.description: The limits the routes apply, so the console does not hard-code them.

expr.description: LogQL. Every stream selector needs an exact match on `service_name`, `namespace` or `job`.

from.description: Epoch ms. Defaults to one hour before `to`.

limit.description: Lines. Capped at 500 rather than refused.

explore_url.description: The same query in Grafana Explore. Null when `GRAFANA_PUBLIC_URL` is unset.

instant.description: Query at `to` instead of over the range.

series.description: The true number of series Mimir returned, before truncation.

data.description: Mimir's response, with `data.result` truncated to `max_series` when needed.
The backend's response verbatim, or null unless `status` is `ok`.

label.description: What the row is, for a heading — e.g. `hashicorp/aws 5.80.0`.

status.description: The D1 row's status. Null for a plan, which has none.

logql.description:
Pins `namespace` as well as the journey id. `tm.*` attributes arrive as structured
metadata, not labels, so filtering on the id alone would read every stream in Loki
first — and would not satisfy the stream-selector guard.

deleted_at.description: Unix ms of the soft delete; `null` = live.

member_count.description: Active members (not those who have left).

PlatformTenantsStorageDomain.title: PlatformTenantsStorageDomain
PlatformTenantsStorageDomain.description:
One storage domain. `measured_bytes` sums the rows whose size was recorded, and is `null`
when rows exist but none is measured (render "unmeasured", not 0 B). `complete` is true
when no row is unmeasured; an empty domain is complete, because its 0 B is a fact.

last_seen_at.description: Last authenticated request by this user anywhere on the platform.

raw_tier.description: The stored column, which can differ from `tier` on a personal tenant.

items.description: Active members first (owners, admins, members, readers), then former members; at most 200.

entitled_providers.description: Providers the org may pull as Terramantle builds.

lockfile_providers.description: Distinct provider addresses across the org's uploaded lock files.

providers_pulled_30d.description: Distinct namespace/type served in the last 30 days.

last_audit_event_at.description: `null` is expected on Starter, which writes no tenant audit events.

providers_entitled.description:
Self-built, unyanked provider bytes this org is entitled to. Shared, not owned:
every entitled org counts the same bytes, so never sum this across tenants.

count.description: Never 0 - a zero day is omitted.

since.description: Unix ms of the UTC midnight opening the first bucket.

PlatformTenantsUsageSeries.title: PlatformTenantsUsageSeries
PlatformTenantsUsageSeries.description: Sparse daily counts, oldest first. An absent day had zero events.

PlatformTenantsUsageTotals.title: PlatformTenantsUsageTotals
PlatformTenantsUsageTotals.description: Sum of each series over the window.

top_modules.description: At most 10 of the tenant's modules by downloads in the window; modules with none are left out.

top_providers.description: At most 10 providers (namespace/type) served to the tenant in the window.

daily_breakdown.description:
The two download series split per day, sparse like `series` (the console zero-fills).
Each sums, day by day, to its total in `series`. They are separate because provider
downloads typically run an order of magnitude above module downloads, so one shared
axis flattens the module line; the console charts each on its own axis instead.

os.description: `null` on rows recorded before os/arch were.

module_downloads_by_actor.description:
Module downloads split by who made them. No user-agent or country is recorded on
download events, so the actor kind is the only client dimension there is.

provider_downloads_by_platform.description: At most 10 os/arch pairs requested. Both are `null` on rows recorded before the platform was captured.

storage.description: The same object as `PlatformTenantsDetail.storage`; not windowed (it is what is retained now).

include_demo.description: `false` (the default) means demo tenants are left out of every number here.

top_tenants.description: At most 10 tenants by `downloads` in the window; tenants with none are left out.

module_downloads.description: Downloads of this tenant's own modules.

provider_downloads.description: Provider binaries served to this tenant.

sub.description: The token subject. For portal tokens this is the user's email (sub_mode user_email).

roles.description: The token's `roles` claim, as the worker read it.

operator.description: Always `true`: a non-operator gets `403`, never `operator: false`.

PolicyInteraction.title: PolicyInteraction
PolicyInteraction.description: What terraform/tofu (or a human acting on its behalf) was doing when the decision was made.

PolicyDecision.title: PolicyDecision
PolicyDecision.description:
One row of the policy decision ledger. `reason` is the message already shown to the client —
policy names and counts, never a resource value out of a plan or state file.

verdict.description:
`block` the interaction was refused; `override` a human lifted or imposed a refusal;
`warn` evaluated and failed, but the policy was not enforcing.

source.description:
Which engine or authority decided — `builtin` the synchronous threshold/denylist plan
gate, `opa` custom Rego, `scan` an enforcing policy result written by a scanner,
`manual` an explicit admin block or approval, `serve_override` a tri-state force.

subject_id.description:
The subject's row id where one resolved. No foreign key: the subject is polymorphic
across five tables, and the ledger must outlive the row it refers to.

subject_key.description:
Machine coordinates for the subject, so a client can build a link to it (migration
128). One of `workspace:<name>`, `state:<workspace>/<versionId>`,
`plan:<workspace>/<planVersionId>`,
`module:<namespace>/<name>/<provider>@<version>`, or
`provider:<registry>/<namespace>/<type>@<version>`.

The provider form carries the resolved registry lineage (`terraform.io` /
`opentofu.org`), never the raw upstream — the provider policy gate is self-built only,
so a key built from the upstream would read `provider:self_built/…` on every policy
refusal and route nowhere.

`null` on a row written before migration 128, and on any row whose coordinates did not
fully resolve. It is NOT derivable from `subject_label`, which is lossy display text (a
module label carries no provider segment). Clients must render the label unlinked when
this is null rather than guessing a route.

run_id.description: state_apply_runs.id when the decision happened inside a lock.

policy_id.description:
Null for the builtin gate and for a manual block, neither of which has a policies row.
Not a foreign key, so deleting a policy does not erase its history.

tool.description: terraform | opentofu | other, from the User-Agent.

req_id.description: Joins to the log line for the same interaction.

trace_id.description: Joins to the trace for the same interaction.

has_more.description:
Whether rows remain beyond this page. Exact, because it is derived from `facets.total`
rather than guessed from the page size — so a client never issues a speculative request
that comes back empty.

daily.description:
Refusals (`verdict = 'block'`) per UTC day over `window_days`, oldest first. SPARSE: a
day with no refusal is omitted and the client zero-fills, so a dip to the axis is a
real gap. Bucketed with `strftime(…, 'unixepoch')`, so the domain the client fills must
be UTC too — a locale domain drops or duplicates a day for every viewer west of UTC.

Honours `policy_id` and `q` so the series agrees with the rows, and ignores `verdict`
and `interaction` (it is a refusal series by definition).

**Present only on the first page (`offset = 0`)** and omitted otherwise: paging cannot
change the series, so recomputing it per page would be pure cost.

PolicyDecisionFacets.title: PolicyDecisionFacets
PolicyDecisionFacets.description:
Counts for the segmented filters, each computed with every filter applied EXCEPT its own
dimension — so a segment reports how many rows you would get if you switched to it with the
other filters held.

Deliberately not whole-window totals: the UI disables a zero-count segment on the grounds
that the bucket holds nothing under the other filters, which a window total would make
untrue. Equally deliberately not counted client-side over the loaded page: overrides are
rare and clustered in time, so one page would report "no overrides" for an org that has
several in the window.

interaction.description: Grouped by interaction, with every filter except `interaction` applied.

verdict.description: Grouped by verdict, with every filter except `verdict` applied.

total.description: Rows matching every filter — the exact count the list is paging through.

window_days.description: Window for block_count only; the verdict counts have no window.

pass_count.description: Artefact versions whose latest stored verdict for this policy passes.

fail_count.description: Artefact versions whose latest stored verdict for this policy fails.

block_count.description: Refusals this policy caused within window_days.

OnMissingSignal.title: OnMissingSignal
OnMissingSignal.description:
How a **missing** trust signal is treated — not a failing one.

Named `signal_fail_gate` before policy-input contract v2; the old spelling is still
ACCEPTED on `PATCH` and still returned on `GET` for one release, because this endpoint is a
documented contract and callers do not deploy alongside the worker. The values are
unchanged.

- `ignore` — fail open. An artefact with no signal is allowed.
- `hard_fail` — fail closed. No signal is treated as a failure.

The highest-consequence field in the policy settings.

PolicyEnablement.title: PolicyEnablement
PolicyEnablement.description:
Which artefact kinds this org evaluates policies for. **Enforcement needs `opaTier` as well
as the toggle** — a toggle on with the tier gate off evaluates and reports but refuses
nothing.

global.description: Master switch. Off ⇒ nothing is enforced for any artefact kind.

opaTier.description:
Whether the org's tier includes custom policies. Read-only here — it comes from
billing, not from this endpoint.

signal_fail_gate.description: Former name of `on_missing_signal`. Returned for one release; do not read it.

allOf.title: PolicySettings
allOf.description: Enablement plus the current blast radius and who last changed it.

modules_blocked_count.description: Module versions currently blocked by an enforcing policy.

last_changed_by.description: Email of whoever last changed these settings, from the audit log.

changed.description:
`false` ⇒ the request changed nothing: no recompute, no rescan, no audit entry,
and the rate limit was not consumed.

rows_changed.description: Artefact rows whose consumability the recompute altered.

blocked.description: Armed — every consume of this artefact type is refused for the whole org.

policy_id.description:
The backing `policies` row, non-null once the switch has ever been armed for this
artefact. Disarming keeps the row so historical decision-ledger entries still resolve
to a policy; `null` means it has never been armed.

changed_at.description:
Only meaningful while `blocked` is true. Once disarmed it is when the switch was turned
**off**, so do not render it as "armed at".

changed_by.description: Email of the owner who last armed or disarmed it.

all_blocked.description:
Derived, not stored: true when all three are armed. There is no master flag in the
database — the UI's master switch reads this and writes `all`.

changed.description:
The artefact types this request actually flipped. Empty ⇒ the request was a no-op:
nothing was written and nothing was audited.

rego.description: The policy body. Always declares `package terramantle.policy`.
